children: Long-term data from two phase 3 studies showed that adults with Crohn's disease treated with Tremfya (guselkumab) saw clinical remission rates of up to 94% over three years.

Participants in the GALAXI 2 and GALAXI 3 trials received Tremfya induction therapy and then either 100 mg every eight weeks or 200 mg every four weeks. Those on the eight-week regimen saw 94% remission; for those on the four-week regimen, the figure was 91%.
Also, 52% of patients in the eight-week regimen group
endoscopic remission, while 61% in the four-week regimen did.
In addition, 88% of patients in both groups saw 90-day corticosteroid-free clinical remission.
Separately, J&J said that results from the phase 3 FUZION study showed that Tremfya led to consistent fistula remission in certain Crohn's subgroups.
Overall, 28% of patients on the eight-week (q8w) regimen and 27% on the four-week (q4w) regimen achieved the composite endpoint of combined fistula remission at week 24 vs. 10% of those on placebo.
However, individuals with greater luminal disease activity at baseline saw 30% and 21% remission, respectively, at q8w and q4w, vs. 0% with placebo.
Patients on Tremfya with prior biologic exposure and those with or without proctitis at baseline also saw
fistula remission compared to those on placebo.

title: J&J long-term Tremfya data demonstrates Crohn's remission through three years
